title: Sell Mineral Rights in Mobile, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Mobile, AL | Colonial Land Grants
metaDescription: Hold a mineral interest tied to old Mobile, AL land, possibly a colonial-era grant? Get a title-researched offer, no pressure to sign anything.
heroLead: Mobile's land records reach back further than almost anywhere else in Alabama, into the French and Spanish colonial grants that predate statehood, and mineral interests tied to that old land can carry title questions no other part of the state has to deal with.
intro: A mineral interest connected to Mobile rarely sits under the city itself — more often it's tied to family land out toward Citronelle, Chunchula, or the rural western part of the county, held by a family whose home has been in Mobile for generations. Because so much of the original land grant history here predates the standard American township-and-range survey system, tracing a legal description back to its source sometimes means working through old Spanish or French grant boundaries before the deed record even starts looking familiar.

sections.heading: When the Land Predates the Grid
paragraphs: Some of the oldest tracts in Mobile County were surveyed under colonial-era grant systems rather than the section-township-range grid used almost everywhere else in Alabama, which can make an old legal description harder to match to a modern parcel. We've done this kind of research before, and we do it ourselves rather than asking a family to hire a surveyor before we'll talk.

sections.heading: The Probate Court Downtown
paragraphs: The Mobile County Probate Court holds the deed and estate records that answer most ownership questions, going back further than in most Alabama counties. Before we make an offer, we pull those records to confirm what your family actually owns and how it's been held since the last clear title transfer.

sections.heading: What We Look At Before Naming a Number
paragraphs: Value depends on where the underlying tract sits relative to producing fields like Citronelle, whether it's ever been leased or drilled, and what any current royalty statement shows. We price against that specific, current information rather than the reputation of Mobile County as an oil-producing area generally.

faqs.question: Our deed references an old Spanish or French land grant. Can you still work with that?
faqs.answer: Yes. We've traced colonial-era legal descriptions before and match them to current parcels ourselves as part of confirming title.

faqs.question: We live in Mobile but the actual mineral interest is out near Citronelle. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: No — we research wherever the tract sits in the county, not where the family currently lives.

faqs.question: How far back do Mobile County's records actually go?
faqs.answer: Further than most Alabama counties, in some cases into the colonial period. That depth of record is usually an advantage in confirming clean title, not an obstacle.
